questions.q: Their carrier takes a short carry. What do our two midfielders do next?
options: The near one moves with the ball; the other keeps covering
Both drop back to the defenders
questions.explain: Yes. Pressure stays on the ball while the cover keeps a second line behind it.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Pressure stays on the ball while the cover keeps a second line behind it.
If both chase, one pass or dribble beats them both and nobody covers behind.
If both drop, nobody slows the carrier, so they can run or pass freely.

questions.q: Which picture shows pressure and cover working together?
questions.explain: Right. One slows the carrier, and the other protects the space behind for the next danger.
choiceExplanations: Both are at the ball, so one pass gets past them and the space behind is empty.
Right. One slows the carrier, and the other protects the space behind for the next danger.
Nobody is close to the ball, so the carrier has time to pick any pass.

questions.q: The central midfielder is nearer and presses this time. You are the other midfielder. Where do you go?
options: Join the press at the ball
questions.explain: Yes. Behind the presser, you cover the next pass or dribble instead of chasing the same ball.
choiceExplanations: Two at the ball means one pass beats you both, and nobody covers the space behind.
Out wide you are too far away to help if the carrier gets past the presser.
Yes. Behind the presser, you cover the next pass or dribble instead of chasing the same ball.
